flashcard_questions.q: Which gland produces FSH and LH?
Which organ produces oestrogen and progesterone?
What does FSH do in the menstrual cycle?
flashcard_questions.a: It causes an egg to mature inside a follicle in the ovary.

flashcard_questions.q: What does a surge in LH trigger?
flashcard_questions.a: Ovulation, the release of a mature egg from the ovary.

flashcard_questions.q: What does oestrogen do to the uterus lining?
flashcard_questions.a: It causes the lining to thicken with blood vessels.

flashcard_questions.q: What does progesterone do to the uterus lining?
flashcard_questions.a: It maintains the thickened lining after ovulation.

flashcard_questions.q: On which day of a 28-day cycle does ovulation usually occur?
Which hormone does rising oestrogen inhibit?
Why does progesterone prevent another egg from being released?
flashcard_questions.a: It inhibits both FSH and LH, so no new follicle matures.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the empty follicle become after ovulation?
flashcard_questions.a: The corpus luteum, which produces progesterone.

flashcard_questions.q: How does the combined contraceptive pill prevent ovulation?
flashcard_questions.a: High oestrogen and progesterone inhibit FSH and LH release.

flashcard_questions.q: How does the progesterone-only pill prevent pregnancy?
flashcard_questions.a: It thickens cervical mucus so sperm cannot reach the egg.

flashcard_questions.q: Which contraceptive method also protects against sexually transmitted infections?
